content.intro: This lesson focuses on http range requests and large resources in advanced api design and distributed architecture. You will connect range requests and partial content to a concrete API contract decision, inspect a small example, and decide what evidence proves the behavior is correct.
content.why_it_matters: HTTP Range Requests and Large Resources matters because API consumers depend on predictable behavior even when clients, servers, networks, and stored data evolve independently. Applying range requests and partial content deliberately reduces ambiguity, makes failures easier to diagnose, and gives tests a clear expectation.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Distributed services introduce partial failure, eventual consistency, and cross-service coordination trade-offs that need explicit design. In this lesson, treat “HTTP Range Requests and Large Resources” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.

Separate a transport failure from an application validation failure, authorization denial, and dependency/database failure.
